reference_findings.diagnosis: Possible unstable angina / NSTE-ACS remains a working diagnosis because symptoms are crescendo/rest symptoms; biomarker-negative results do not alone exclude unstable angina. Non-cardiac causes remain in differential.
reference_findings.risk_assessment: High concern / urgent assessment; qualitative simulation label only, not a validated score.

investigation_reports.ecg: Sinus rhythm; nonspecific ST-T changes; no diagnostic ST elevation. Repeat ECG during recurrent symptoms is not yet available.
investigation_reports.laboratory_panel: hs-cTn fictional assay: 0 h below 99th percentile; repeat sample at scenario-defined interval remains below threshold without significant delta. CBC without major abnormality; creatinine 0.9 mg/dL; potassium 4.1 mmol/L; glucose 118 mg/dL. These are synthetic values.
investigation_reports.echocardiography: LVEF 55%; no definite regional wall-motion abnormality; no significant pericardial effusion. Image quality adequate in this teaching report.
investigation_reports.coronary_or_other_imaging: No coronary anatomy study supplied at entry. If invasive angiography is selected in the reference branch, it shows mild diffuse plaque with no focal stenosis >50% and TIMI 3 flow in all major vessels.
investigation_reports.initial_vitals: HR 88 bpm; BP 142/84 mmHg; RR 18/min; SpO2 98% room air; temperature 36.8 C; alert, no shock signs in initial snapshot.
investigation_reports.not_supplied: Any test not explicitly listed is not ordered/not available; it must not be interpreted as normal.

history.chief_complaint: New chest pressure at rest lasting 12 minutes, resolved before assessment; two similar episodes over 24 hours.
history.history_of_present_illness: Central pressure with radiation to left shoulder; no fever or pleuritic component reported. Symptom pattern is new and increasing in frequency.
relevant_history: No known prior MI or coronary intervention
medication_reconciliation: Fictional home list: antihypertensive and lipid-lowering therapy; exact names/adherence to be reconciled
allergy_history: No known drug allergy recorded in this scenario; verify directly rather than assuming absence

differential_diagnosis: Pulmonary cause if symptoms/signs support it

pathway_review.label: Urgent clinical assessment, serial ECG/biomarkers and risk-based disposition
pathway_review.reason: Crescendo/rest symptoms require careful assessment even with initially negative biomarkers.

pathway_review.label: Specialist-led invasive evaluation if risk profile or recurrence supports it
pathway_review.reason: Choice depends on full risk assessment, recurrence, local pathway and patient factors.

pathway_review.label: Discharge based only on one normal ECG and one negative troponin
pathway_review.reason: Ignores symptom trajectory and limitations of single time-point testing.

reference_findings.safety_review: Confirm symptom onset and serial testing timing; reconcile medicines; document allergy details; assess renal function, bleeding risk, pregnancy possibility where relevant, consent and escalation plan before any invasive pathway.
reference_findings.simulated_clinical_course: Reference branch: no culprit obstructive lesion found; learner receives a debrief on why the diagnosis remains clinical and why no automatic PCI target exists.
learning_objectives: Distinguish unstable angina from biomarker-positive MI without overclaiming certainty.
Use serial testing and clinical trajectory.
Avoid automatic angiography or PCI without a reasoned indication.
reference_findings.review_note: Synthetic scenario. Clinical values and pathway labels require qualified interventional cardiology review before deployment. Educational use only; not real-patient guidance.
